chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.'

What is the 'way'? He said: 'That he has what he performs the pilgrimage with.' I said: 'If something is presented to him for his pilgrimage and he feels shy of it, is he among those who are able to find a way to it?' He said: 'Yes, what is his shyness about? Even if he performs the pilgrimage on a donkey with a cut tail. And if he is able to walk part of the way and ride part of it, let him perform the pilgrimage.'

key_terms.حِمَارٍ أَبْتَرَ: A donkey with a cut tail (indicating any available mount, regardless of quality)
key_terms.مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا: Whoever is able to find a way to it

ai.seo_question: What constitutes the 'ability' required for the obligatory Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Halabi, transmitted through the chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, clarifies that 'ability' (istita'ah) refers to the possession of sufficient means rather than physical perfection, as evidenced by the Prophet's allowance for Hajj even on a 'mutilated donkey.' It further establishes that modesty (haya') regarding one's wealth does not negate the obligation, and partial capacity—such as walking part of the journey and riding the rest—is sufficient to fulfill the duty. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the flexibility of financial and physical prerequisites for Hajj.
